chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
We are the pillow in the middle. He who lags behind has to come forward to meet it while he who has exceeded the bounds has to return to it.

key_terms.التَّالِى: The one who lags behind, falls short, or is deficient.
key_terms.النُّمْرُقَةُ: A small pillow or cushion placed between the head and the bed, used here as a metaphor for a central, supportive pillar.
key_terms.الْغَالِى: The one who exceeds, goes beyond the limit, or transgresses.
key_terms.الْوُسْطَى: The middle, the central, or the median.

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the 'pillow' metaphor in Nahj al-Balagha regarding the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: In this metaphor from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) identifies the Ahl al-Bayt as 'an-nimruqah al-wusta' (the middle pillow), symbolizing their role as the essential intermediary between the divine and the community. This imagery underscores the Shia doctrine of *al-wasatiyyah* (centrality), where the Imams serve as the stable reference point that corrects those who lag behind in understanding and grounds those who exceed in excess, ensuring the community remains on the straight path.
